All confirmed. Every path to obtain the `store.Driver` implementation goes through `store/db/db.go`'s `NewDBDriver` factory, which is the only place that imports/calls `store/db/mysql.NewDB`.

The only other place `"mysql"` appears as a `sql.Open` driver name is `store/test/containers.go`, but that uses the raw `database/sql` + `github.com/go-sql-driver/mysql` driver directly for test-infrastructure purposes (creating throwaway test databases and polling readiness) — it does not construct the application's `store/db/mysql.DB` (the `store.Driver` implementation).

No; evidence

The driver-selection factory is `store/db/db.go`'s `NewDBDriver`, which is the only place in the codebase that imports `github.com/usememos/memos/store/db/mysql` and calls its constructor:

```8:22:/bench/repo/store/db/db.go
	"github.com/usememos/memos/store/db/mysql"
	"github.com/usememos/memos/store/db/postgres"
	"github.com/usememos/memos/store/db/sqlite"
)

// NewDBDriver creates new db driver based on profile.
func NewDBDriver(profile *profile.Profile) (store.Driver, error) {
	var driver store.Driver
	var err error

	switch profile.Driver {
	case "sqlite":
		driver, err = sqlite.NewDB(profile)
	case "mysql":
		driver, err = mysql.NewDB(profile)
```

Checks performed:
- `grep -rn "mysql.NewDB\|db/mysql\""` across all `.go` files returns only `store/db/db.go` (two matches, both in that one file). No other file imports the `store/db/mysql` package or calls `mysql.NewDB`.
- `grep -rn "mysql\.DB{"` (looking for direct struct literal construction of the `mysql.DB` type) returns no results anywhere.
- All callers that obtain a MySQL-capable `store.Driver` do so exclusively via `db.NewDBDriver(...)`: `cmd/memos/main.go:57`, `server/router/api/v1/test/memo_service_benchmark_test.go:70`, and `store/test/store.go:28,50`. None of these import or reference `store/db/mysql` directly.

The one MySQL-adjacent usage outside this factory is in `store/test/containers.go`, which calls `sql.Open("mysql", dsn)` directly (via the raw `database/sql` + `github.com/go-sql-driver/mysql` driver) purely to create/verify throwaway test databases in a Docker container — it does not construct the application's `store/db/mysql.DB` (the `store.Driver` implementation), so it doesn't count as constructing "the MySQL driver" in the sense of the app's driver abstraction.
